Abstract base class for Adafruit graphics devices. Provides drawing primitives, text rendering, rotation, and buffer-agnostic API. Subclasses must implement drawPixel and may override write* and control APIs. Manages state like dimensions, cursor, text colors/sizes, rotation, and optional GFXfont. Construction requires width and height; destruction/ownership notes are not specified here.

Lightweight UI button helper that uses an Adafruit_GFX drawing context to render itself and track pressed state. Initialized via initButton or initButtonUL, can draw and hit-test, and provides edge-triggered state queries. It does not own the Adafruit_GFX pointer.

Off-screen 1-bit-per-pixel canvas implementing Adafruit_GFX. Maintains an internal byte buffer (optionally allocated) and provides pixel, line, and fill operations. Destructor frees buffer only if buffer_owned is true. getBuffer exposes raw raster data for blitting.

Off-screen 8-bits-per-pixel canvas implementing Adafruit_GFX. Internal linear buffer holds one byte per pixel; supports draw/fill/line operations and exposes the buffer pointer. Destructor frees buffer only when buffer_owned is true.

Off-screen 16-bits-per-pixel canvas implementing Adafruit_GFX, typically RGB565. Provides pixel/line/fill operations, byteSwap for endian correction, and exposes the 16-bit buffer. Destructor frees buffer if buffer_owned is true.

Intermediary graphics/display driver base class between Adafruit_GFX and hardware-specific display subclasses. Provides SPI and parallel bus handling, windowing, pixel drawing, DMA support (on some MCUs), and optimized pin toggling. Subclasses must implement begin() and setAddrWindow().

Abstract base class providing generic grayscale OLED display support atop Adafruit_GFX. It manages an internal framebuffer, I2C/SPI transport via Adafruit_I2CDevice/Adafruit_SPIDevice, and common operations (clear, invert, contrast, drawPixel, getPixel). Subclasses must implement display() to transfer the buffer to the hardware. Multiple constructors support I2C, software SPI, or hardware SPI. Lifetime ownership of spi_dev/i2c_dev and buffer is implied but destruction details are not shown in this header.

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::initSPI
functions.signature: void Adafruit_SPITFT::initSPI(uint32_t freq = 0, uint8_t spiMode = SPI_MODE0)

requirements: Must be called by subclass begin() during initialization
spiMode must be a valid SPI_MODEn constant defined by SPI.h
freq is in Hz; 0 selects a platform default speed

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::setSPISpeed
functions.description: Sets the SPI bus speed used for subsequent transactions to freq Hz.
requirements: freq is in Hz; caller should choose a value supported by both MCU and display

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::startWrite
functions.description: Begins a low-level write transaction: asserts chip-select and/or starts a hardware SPI transaction as needed. Intended to bracket a sequence of write* operations for efficiency.
requirements: Must be balanced with a corresponding endWrite()
Do not assume reentrancy or nesting; call patterns should be non-nested unless the implementation explicitly supports it (not documented)

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::endWrite

requirements: Must be preceded by a matching startWrite()

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::sendCommand
functions.signature: void Adafruit_SPITFT::sendCommand(uint8_t commandByte, uint8_t *dataBytes, uint8_t numDataBytes)

requirements: If numDataBytes > 0, dataBytes must point to a buffer of at least numDataBytes bytes

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::sendCommand16
functions.signature: void Adafruit_SPITFT::sendCommand16(uint16_t commandWord, const uint8_t *dataBytes = NULL, uint8_t numDataBytes = 0)

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::readcommand8

requirements: commandByte must be a valid command for the target display
index selects which byte of the response to return (0-based); behavior for out-of-range index is implementation-defined

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::readcommand16

requirements: addr must be a valid 16-bit command/address for the target display controller

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::writePixel
functions.signature: void Adafruit_SPITFT::writePixel(int16_t x, int16_t y, uint16_t color)
functions.description: Writes a single pixel of the given 16-bit color to coordinates (x, y). Intended for use inside an active write transaction.
requirements: Typically call after startWrite() and appropriate setAddrWindow() for best performance

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::writePixels
functions.signature: void Adafruit_SPITFT::writePixels(uint16_t *colors, uint32_t len, bool block = true, bool bigEndian = false)
functions.description: Writes a sequence of len pixels from the colors buffer to the display. May support non-blocking DMA on some platforms; block controls whether the call waits for completion. bigEndian indicates the byte order of the input pixel data.
requirements: colors must point to a buffer containing at least len 16-bit RGB565 pixels
len is the number of pixels to write

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::writeColor

requirements: len specifies the number of pixels to write

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::writeFillRect

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::writeFastHLine
functions.signature: void Adafruit_SPITFT::writeFastHLine(int16_t x, int16_t y, int16_t w, uint16_t color)

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::writeFastVLine
functions.signature: void Adafruit_SPITFT::writeFastVLine(int16_t x, int16_t y, int16_t h, uint16_t color)

functions.description: Fills a rectangle where all arguments are already sorted, clipped, and guaranteed onscreen. Provides a faster path by skipping checks. Calling with unclipped or negative values may be disastrous per the comments.

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::dmaWait
functions.description: Blocks until any in-progress DMA transfer initiated by writePixels or internal fills completes. On platforms without DMA, this may be a no-op.

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::dmaBusy
functions.description: Returns true if a DMA transfer is currently in progress and false otherwise. If DMA is not used, returns false.

functions.name: Adafruit_SPITFT::swapBytes

functions.description: Swaps the byte order of len 16-bit values. If dest is NULL, the swap may be performed in-place on src; otherwise, writes swapped results to dest.
requirements: src must point to a buffer with at least len 16-bit elements

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::Adafruit_GrayOLED
functions.signature: Adafruit_GrayOLED::Adafruit_GrayOLED(uint8_t bpp, uint16_t w, uint16_t h, TwoWire *twi = &Wire, int16_t rst_pin = -1, uint32_t preclk = 400000, uint32_t postclk = 100000)

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::~Adafruit_GrayOLED

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::clearDisplay
functions.description: Clears the internal framebuffer for the display, setting all pixels to off. Does not automatically send data to the display; call display() to apply changes.
requirements: A valid framebuffer must be allocated (normally after subclass/device initialization).

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::invertDisplay
functions.description: Sets the display inversion mode. When enabled, the display renders colors inverted per device capability.
requirements: The device must be initialized and communication established before calling.
Parameter i selects inverted (true) or normal (false) mode.

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::setContrast
functions.description: Adjusts the OLED contrast setting by sending the generic contrast command, where supported by the hardware.
requirements: Device must be initialized and able to receive commands.
contrastlevel is an 8-bit value (0–255); valid range may be further constrained by the specific controller (details unknown).

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::drawPixel
functions.signature: void Adafruit_GrayOLED::drawPixel(int16_t x, int16_t y, uint16_t color)
functions.description: Plots a single pixel into the internal framebuffer at (x, y) with the specified color. Does not immediately update the physical display; call display() to flush.
requirements: x must be within [0, width-1] and y within [0, height-1] of the display; pixels outside the bounds are ignored or clipped per implementation (exact behavior unknown).

A valid framebuffer must be allocated (normally after subclass/device initialization).

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::getPixel
functions.description: Returns the current on/off state of a pixel at (x, y) from the internal framebuffer. For grayscale modes, return represents a boolean interpretation (nonzero treated as on).
requirements: x must be within [0, width-1] and y within [0, height-1]; out-of-bounds behavior is implementation-defined (details unknown).

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::getBuffer
functions.description: Provides a pointer to the internal 1:1 framebuffer backing the display. Useful for bulk operations or DMA-like transfers by subclasses.
requirements: A framebuffer must have been allocated by the device/subclass initialization before calling; otherwise this may return null.

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::oled_command
functions.description: Sends a single command byte to the OLED controller over the configured bus (I2C or SPI). Intended for low-level control sequences by subclasses or advanced users.
requirements: The device/bus must be initialized and configured via the appropriate constructor and subsequent init routine.

functions.name: Adafruit_GrayOLED::oled_commandList
functions.description: Sends a list of n command bytes to the OLED controller. Useful for issuing initialization or configuration sequences.
requirements: The device/bus must be initialized and ready to receive commands.
c must point to a buffer containing at least n bytes of command data; the pointer must remain valid for the duration of the call.
n is the number of command bytes to transmit; must accurately reflect the size of the command list.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: ASCII label (<=9 chars)
# Fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a label that is then truncated to 9 chars
# and sanitized for NULs. They also request several unsigned ints for geometry/colors.
# Our single returned bytes buffer should therefore contain:
# - A short ASCII label (<=9 visible chars, no NULs) terminated by a newline so the fuzzer's
#   string extractor can consume a self-contained string region.
# - Followed by a sequence of 32-bit unsigned integers to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
#   calls in the order they appear in the stubs. Each stub uses multiple FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int):
#   x, y, w, h, outline, fill, textcolor, textsize seed. We provide enough values to support both
#   initButton and initButtonUL paths.
# - We will pack numbers in little-endian to be broadly compatible.
#
# Strategy:
# - Generate a label of length 1..9 with a mix of printable characters, including spaces and digits.
# - Generate geometry-related numbers tailored to typical ranges to encourage diverse behavior.
#   Although the stubs mod these by gfx->width()/height(), we still vary them widely.
# - Provide two full parameter sets back-to-back so both stubs can draw from the buffer.
# - Keep total size well under 4096 bytes.

PRINTABLE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " !@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:'\",.<>/?|`~"
)

def _u32le(n: int) -> bytes:
    n &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF, (n >> 16) & 0xFF, (n >> 24) & 0xFF))

def _rand_color(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # 16-bit color will be truncated from the u32; still provide varied lower 16 bits.
    return rng.getrandbits(16) | (rng.randrange(0, 0x10000) << 16)

def _param_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce eight unsigned ints for: x, y, w, h, outline, fill, textcolor, textsize_seed
    buf = bytearray()
    # x, y arbitrary; will be modulo display size
    buf += _u32le(rng.getrandbits(32))
    buf += _u32le(rng.getrandbits(32))
    # w, h positive after modulo+1; choose values favoring small and larger sizes
    def biased_dimension():
        choice = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            return rng.randrange(1, 16)  # tiny
        elif choice == 1:
            return rng.randrange(16, 129)  # small/medium
        elif choice == 2:
            return rng.randrange(129, 1024)  # big
        else:
            return rng.getrandbits(32)  # random wide
    buf += _u32le(biased_dimension())
    buf += _u32le(biased_dimension())
    # outline, fill, textcolor (16-bit meaningful)
    buf += _u32le(_rand_color(rng))
    buf += _u32le(_rand_color(rng))
    buf += _u32le(_rand_color(rng))
    # textsize seed -> modulo 5 + 1 in stub; vary it
    buf += _u32le(rng.randrange(0, 256))
    return bytes(buf)

def _make_label(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Length 1..9
    L = rng.randrange(1, 10)
    # Ensure variety: sometimes numeric, sometimes mixed, include spaces/punct
    label_chars: List[str] = []
    for i in range(L):
        label_chars.append(rng.choice(PRINTABLE))
    # Avoid embedded NUL by construction; the fuzzer sanitizes anyway
    return ''.join(label_chars)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()

    # Compose 2-3 labels to allow multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers if present.
    label_count = 2 if rng.random() < 0.75 else 3
    for i in range(label_count):
        label = _make_label(rng)
        out += label.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
        out += b"\n"  # delimiter to help string extraction routines

    # Add two full parameter blocks for the two stubs
    out += _param_block(rng)
    out += _param_block(rng)

    # Add an extra block to provide surplus ints for any additional calls
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        out += _param_block(rng)

    # Ensure size limit
    return bytes(out[:4096])
